summary.headline: WPIL Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell 11% YoY to INR511 crore, while FY26 revenue grew 3% to INR1,855 crore and EBITDA margin reached 17.16%.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue declined 11% YoY to INR511 crore, with PAT from continuing operations flat at INR47 crore. For full FY26, consolidated revenue rose 3% to INR1,855 crore, EBITDA rose 9% to INR318 crore, and margin was 17.16%. Standalone revenue fell 34% in FY26 to INR763 crore, as the India project business was weak amid delayed Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) funds; international revenue rose to INR1,136 crore. Management highlighted a South African order book of about ZAR4 billion (announced after the period end) and renewed JJM 2 momentum.

segments.name: Products (domestic)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR109 crore vs INR108 crore last year. Product order backlog INR5,796 million at FY26-end; India products grew about 15% and international products about 5% in FY26 per analyst computation, with total product growth about 10%.

segments.name: Projects (domestic)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR92 crore vs INR253 crore last year, as the company focused on commissioning and starting O&M. India project order book about INR2,000 crore, of which about INR500 crore O&M and about INR1,450 crore EPC (31 March 2026).

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: FY26 international revenue INR1,136 crore vs INR668 crore; international EBITDA rose to INR152 crore from INR88 crore. Management said international was about 65% of revenue and domestic about 35%. WPIL Thailand JV crossed INR300 crore revenue for the first time.

segments.name: South Africa (PCI Africa, Eigenbau)
segments.commentary: Record revenue and profitability at Eigenbau; PCI Africa won City of Cape Town contracts (Maccasar, Lower Umkhomazi). Post period-end order of about ZAR4 billion (INR ~1,800 crore routed via PCI) with 36-48 month execution. PCI Africa was acquired mid-FY25, so FY26 had a full year versus about 9-10 months in FY25.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to quantify FY27 revenue; said growth is expected, with product growth, JJM 2 fund release, and South African project execution as drivers.
Company-wide EBITDA margin mandate is 15%-20%; management said FY27 margins should be on the higher side of that band.
International mix expected to stay at 60%-65% of revenue.
JJM 2 expected to gain momentum by Q2 FY27; JJM 2 end date 28 December with a roughly 30-month window.
Peak South Africa revenue expected in year 2 of execution as a thumb rule; momentum expected from H2 FY27.
Only small brownfield capex needed for India product capacity.
capex_capacity: Management sees little capex demand; small brownfield additions planned for India product capacity growth.

Order book about INR6,000 crore including South Africa, with the project business about INR5,000 crore and product about INR1,000 crore (as stated by management on the call; the split is inconsistent with other figures given in the call).
Standalone order book shown in presentation: product about INR984 crore and project about INR3,900 crore (per analyst citation, as of 31 March).
Under O&M component of order book about INR530 crore (management said INR550 crore or something).
demand_pricing: JJM backlog about INR1,100 crore from JJM; total order backlog about INR1,400 crore; JJM receivables overdue about INR350 crore; JJM funds not yet released, with releases expected from the current quarter.
Consolidated trade receivables rose from INR820 crore (Mar-25) to INR1,184 crore (Mar-26), attributed mainly to JJM.
Recent orders: DVC and Deepak Chemicals cooling water pump contracts; power, industrial and water sectors are demand drivers.
Raw material (stainless steel, sourced largely from the Gulf) prices volatile; management said no firm view yet.
Consolidated gross margin reportedly fell from about 76% to 71% in Q4 (analyst figure); management attributed margin swings to product/project/country mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total order book, including South Africa, and its execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR6,000 crore company-wide, including about ZAR4 billion from South Africa, executed over 36-48 months. The South Africa order was dated 31 March but received after period-end.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the trade receivable increase relates to JJM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said overdue JJM receivables are about INR350 crore, with the rest invoiced and in process. Fund release is expected from this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did consolidated EBITDA margin decline in Q4, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly margins are volatile due to revenue timing and project site costs, and urged a view over the full year. The India EBITDA margin was about 21% and international about 13% in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is the NSE listing permanent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said WPIL has not yet applied for listing, pending a capital condition that requires raising funds; the resolution has been passed and an application is expected soon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Rutschi tax refund?
qa_highlights.answer: Appeals have been filed and litigation is ongoing; advisers are confident, but resolution could take about 18 months and management could not assure receipt of money.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the authorised capital increased?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is pursuing strategic acquisitions at reasonable valuations and the enabling resolution gives room for that; it did not confirm a fundraise.

risks_watch: JJM fund release timing and receivable collection (about INR350 crore overdue); management said releases should begin this quarter.
Q4 project revenue fell to INR92 crore from INR253 crore; India project pipeline described as low until new water tenders are issued.
Raw material cost volatility (stainless steel) affecting product and project margins.
Rupee depreciation: management cited a foreign exchange gain, with consolidated exchange difference of INR139 crore.
Contract termination dispute under arbitration, which management said is moving slowly.
NSE listing not yet applied for; capital condition pending fundraise.
Sizeable rise in receivables and dependence on South Africa execution timing (peak revenue expected in year 2).
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the outlook, especially South Africa orders and JJM 2, but evasive when asked for quantified FY27 revenue or margin guidance. Repeatedly deferred numbers to later updates and said quarterly margins should not be extrapolated.
key_quotes: So, I think time frame is the only challenge.
We are much higher margin, much better margin we have got there.
So, you should conclude, as I said, that you cannot take 1 quarter and one area as a benchmark and extrapolate because it's quite fluctuating depending on revenues.

adds.what: Small brownfield addition for India product capacity (no size or capex quantified)

growth.why: Management declined to quantify FY27 revenue but said growth is expected from product growth, JJM 2 fund release (momentum by Q2 FY27) and South African project execution (ZAR4 billion order book, peak in year 2, momentum from H2 FY27), backed by order book and only small brownfield capex.
